testName: Class B Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: Is it allowed to send text messages while driving?

options.text: Yes, if the messages are short.
Yes, if you are asking your employer a question.

questions.explanation: You cannot send or read text messages while driving.

questions.question: What is sleep debt?

options.text: When you do not get enough sleep.
When you want to take a nap.
The time it takes to wake up and be ready to drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you do not get enough sleep.
questions.explanation: Sleep debt happens when you do not sleep enough. You can only pay back this debt by getting more sleep.

questions.question: What can happen if you press and release the brake pedal too many times?

options.text: Air leaves the brake system faster than the compressor can replace it.
More air is added to the brake system.
The brake pedal becomes more sensitive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Air leaves the brake system faster than the compressor can replace it.
questions.explanation: In an air brake system, pressing and releasing the brake pedal too many times can cause air to leave faster than the compressor can refill it.

questions.question: What can a modulating control valve control?
questions.explanation: A modulating control valve lets the driver slowly apply spring brakes. A lever on the dashboard controls it in vehicles that have this feature.

questions.question: What should you check during a vehicle inspection?

options.text: Emergency exits are hard to open.
Emergency exits cannot be opened from inside.

questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection, check that emergency exit warning devices work. All emergency exits should open smoothly, be undamaged, and close securely from inside.

questions.question: Should you use a helper when backing?

options.text: No, a helper usually causes confusion.
Only if you are not feeling confident.
No, a helper gets in the way.

questions.explanation: Backing is always dangerous because you cannot see everything behind your vehicle. Whenever possible, use a helper to watch your blind spots.

questions.question: What is the best way to check your lights during a pre-trip inspection?

options.text: Park near a mirror and look for a reflection.
Turn on the lights, then get out and look at them.
Look at the instrument panel to see if warning lights are on.
Drive in traffic and wait for other drivers to tell you if your lights are out.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on the lights, then get out and look at them.
questions.explanation: During a pre-trip inspection, turn on your lights and get out of the vehicle to check them.

questions.question: Which crime would NOT disqualify you from getting a hazardous materials endorsement?
questions.explanation: Certain crimes disqualify you from a hazardous materials endorsement for seven years. These include arson, robbery, and dishonesty. Serious crimes like murder result in a lifetime disqualification. Littering is not one of these crimes.

questions.question: What must you do to check automatic transmission fluid in some vehicles?
questions.explanation: In some vehicles, you must leave the engine running to check the automatic transmission fluid level correctly.

questions.question: What does a high center of gravity do?

options.text: Makes a vehicle more likely to roll over.

questions.correctAnswerText: Makes a vehicle more likely to roll over.
questions.explanation: A high center of gravity makes a vehicle more likely to tip over.

questions.question: Why should you use flares with caution after an accident?

options.text: Spilled fuel on the ground could catch fire.
Other drivers may not see the flares in sunny weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Spilled fuel on the ground could catch fire.
questions.explanation: Vehicle fires can happen after accidents if flares are used near spilled fuel. Always use flares carefully.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in fog?
questions.explanation: If you must drive in fog, reduce your speed. This helps you see better and stop safely.

questions.question: How can you avoid slowing down traffic when driving a large truck?

options.text: Try to pass another vehicle while driving uphill.
Stay in the right lane whenever possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in the right lane whenever possible.
questions.explanation: If your truck cannot keep up with other traffic, stay in the right lane. This allows faster vehicles to pass you safely.

questions.question: If your vehicle catches fire, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Park away from buildings, trees, brush, and other vehicles.
Call emergency services and tell them your location.

questions.explanation: Leave the road and stop in an open area away from other vehicles. Do not go to a service station because fuel there could catch fire. Call emergency services and report your location.

questions.question: What will the examiner grade you on during the driving test?

options.text: How quickly you reach your destination.

questions.explanation: The examiner grades you on specific driving maneuvers and overall driving behavior. You must drive safely, obey all traffic signs and laws, and avoid accidents and moving violations.

questions.question: Why are ice cream trucks hazardous to other drivers?

options.text: Ice cream trucks need to stay cold.
Children often run toward them without looking for traffic.
Ice cream trucks leave water and ice on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Children often run toward them without looking for traffic.
questions.explanation: Ice cream trucks are dangerous because they attract children. Children may run into the street without checking for vehicles.

questions.question: If your brakes fail on a downhill slope, what is your best option to stop?
questions.explanation: An escape ramp is the safest way to stop your vehicle if your brakes fail going downhill.

questions.question: Which behavior shows you may be an aggressive driver?

options.text: Slowing down and staying a safe distance behind other vehicles.
Making hand gestures that could upset other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Making hand gestures that could upset other drivers.
questions.explanation: Avoid aggressive driving by planning for delays, keeping a safe following distance, and not making gestures that could anger other drivers.

questions.question: What should happen when you start an engine?

options.text: Warning lights should turn on and then quickly turn off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning lights should turn on and then quickly turn off.
questions.explanation: When you start your vehicle, warning lights and sounds should stop after a few seconds. If they don't, your vehicle may have a problem.

questions.question: Which is NOT a good rule for using turn signals?

options.text: Signal early, well before you turn or change lanes.
Keep signaling until the turn or lane change is complete.
Don't signal if no one is nearby.

questions.correctAnswerText: Don't signal if no one is nearby.
questions.explanation: Always signal before turning or changing lanes. Signal early, keep signaling throughout the move, and turn off the signal after you are done. Always signal, even if you think no one is nearby.

questions.question: When is drowsy driving most common?
questions.explanation: Drowsy driving happens most at night. Your body is naturally less alert during hours when you normally sleep. If you drive at night, take steps to prevent fatigue.

questions.question: How many driver licenses can one person have?

options.text: Two—one for cars and one for trucks.
One for each state where they plan to drive.
A car license from one state and a CDL from another.

questions.explanation: You can have only one license. States share driver information in a database to prevent duplicate licenses.

questions.question: If you are convicted of a traffic violation, what should you do?

options.text: The state will tell your employer.

questions.explanation: You must notify your employer within 30 days of any traffic conviction, regardless of the vehicle type. You must also tell your motor vehicle licensing agency within 30 days if the conviction happened in another state. Parking tickets do not require notification.

questions.question: What is safe to do with the radiator cap?

options.text: Do not remove it when the coolant is hot.
You can remove it when the coolant is hot.
It should be cool to touch during normal driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not remove it when the coolant is hot.
questions.explanation: Never remove the radiator cap or any part of the cooling system until it cools down. Opening it while hot could release steam and boiling water that can burn you badly. If the cap is cool to touch, the system is safe to open.

questions.question: When backing up with a trailer, what should you do first?

options.text: Turn the steering wheel toward the direction of the turn.
Turn the steering wheel away from the direction of the turn.
Turn the wheel as sharp as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the steering wheel away from the direction of the turn.
questions.explanation: When backing with a trailer, first turn the wheel away from the direction you want the trailer to go. Once the trailer starts turning, reverse the wheel direction to follow it.

questions.question: What do header boards do?

options.text: Protect drivers from cargo that shifts or moves.
Protect drivers' heads when entering the cab.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protect drivers from cargo that shifts or moves.
questions.explanation: A header board protects the driver from cargo moving forward during a crash or emergency stop.

questions.question: Are rims with welding repairs safe to use?

options.text: Yes, they are okay on rear tires.
Yes, only when carrying heavy loads.

questions.explanation: Check your wheels and rims before every trip. Wheels or rims that have been welded are not safe and should not be used.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT something you should check during a pre-trip inspection?

options.text: Tires with too much air pressure.
Tires that are worn too much.

questions.explanation: Check your tires for proper tread depth, cracks, correct air pressure, and equal size. Front tires need at least 4/32 inch tread. Other tires need at least 2/32 inch tread. You do not need to check if tires are from different makers.

questions.question: During straight line backing, how many times can you exit the vehicle to check position?
questions.explanation: During straight line backing, you can exit your vehicle to check position only once.

questions.question: When double clutching, if you stay in neutral too long and can't shift to the next gear, what should you do?

options.text: Stop the vehicle and start over.
Return to neutral, release the clutch, speed up, and try again.
Skip the gear you wanted and go to the next one.

questions.correctAnswerText: Return to neutral, release the clutch, speed up, and try again.
questions.explanation: If you stay in neutral too long while double clutching and can't shift, don't force it. Go back to neutral, release the clutch, increase engine speed to match road speed, and try again.

questions.question: What is traction?

options.text: Grip between your tires and the road
How long it takes to stop when you brake

questions.correctAnswerText: Grip between your tires and the road
questions.explanation: Traction is the grip between your tires and the road. Good traction helps you brake and steer safely.

questions.question: Which is NOT a good way to spot vehicle problems?

options.text: Check important items only at the start and end of a trip

questions.correctAnswerText: Check important items only at the start and end of a trip
questions.explanation: Check your vehicle often during a trip. Watch the gauges, mirrors, tires, cargo, and lights. Use all your senses to catch problems early.

questions.question: What is the safest speed in heavy traffic?

options.text: The same speed as other cars around you
Much slower than the other cars

questions.correctAnswerText: The same speed as other cars around you
questions.explanation: Match the speed of traffic around you. Cars moving at the same speed are less likely to crash. Never exceed the speed limit.

questions.question: What should you know about railroad crossings?

options.text: You will always hear a train coming
You might not hear a train, even if one is coming
A train always sounds two short horn blasts if it is coming

questions.correctAnswerText: You might not hear a train, even if one is coming
questions.explanation: Do not count on hearing a train. The operator may not sound the horn, or it may be against the rules in that area. Noise in your vehicle can also prevent you from hearing a train until it is too close.

questions.question: If you find something unsafe during a pre-trip check, what should you do?

options.text: Drive anyway and see a mechanic later
Let someone more experienced drive instead
Avoid using that part, but drive normally otherwise

questions.explanation: Fix any unsafe problem before you drive. It is against the law to drive an unsafe vehicle.

questions.question: What does the air compressor governor do when air tanks reach 125 psi?

options.text: Start pumping air into the tanks

questions.explanation: The governor stops the compressor when air reaches about 125 psi. This level is called the "cut-out" level.

questions.question: When checking air and electrical lines, which should NOT be true?

options.text: The air hoses and electrical lines are not cut
The air lines are not pinched
The air lines are not dragging against parts

questions.explanation: Listen for leaks in air hoses. Lines should not be cut, worn, tangled, pinched, or dragging. A hissing sound means there is a leak.

questions.question: Why is it most important to check your vehicle before a trip?
questions.explanation: The main reason to check your vehicle is to keep you and others safe on the road. Pre-trip inspections are required by law.

questions.question: What can affect how long it takes to stop?
questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on how fast you are going, how heavy your vehicle is, and how slippery the road is.

questions.question: What is true about a tired driver?

options.text: They should take over-the-counter pills to stay awake
They react to danger too slowly
They drive better than most drivers

questions.correctAnswerText: They react to danger too slowly
questions.explanation: When tired, you cannot see or react to hazards as fast. You will make bad decisions and be a dangerous driver.

questions.question: When driving downhill, a vehicle's speed will likely:
questions.explanation: Gravity pulls a vehicle faster when going downhill, so speed increases.

questions.question: If you notice a safety or mechanical problem while driving, you should:

options.text: Say nothing and hope the problem goes away.
Write a report describing the problem.
Avoid using that part and hope no one notices.

questions.correctAnswerText: Write a report describing the problem.
questions.explanation: At the end of each driving day, you may need to write a report about any vehicle problems. Report anything that could affect safety or cause a breakdown.

questions.question: The more alcohol in your body:

options.text: The faster your liver will break it down.
The less effect it will have.
The longer it will take to leave your body.

questions.correctAnswerText: The longer it will take to leave your body.
questions.explanation: Your body removes alcohol at a fixed rate. More alcohol means it takes longer for your body to remove it.

questions.question: When driving past parked cars, you should:

options.text: Watch for people getting out of parked cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for people getting out of parked cars.
questions.explanation: Someone may suddenly exit a parked car or step out from between cars without looking. A driver might also start their vehicle without seeing you.

questions.question: When you press the brake pedal in a vehicle with S-cam brakes, air pressure pushes out the rod and moves the:
questions.explanation: When you press the brake pedal, air enters the brake chambers. This pressure pushes the rods out and moves the slack adjusters, which twist the brake camshafts.

questions.question: Which of these is a good rule for making a turn?

options.text: Use your arms to signal other drivers.
Turn off your turn signal before entering the turn.

questions.explanation: Signal well before you turn so drivers behind you know what you plan to do. Keep the signal on during the turn and turn it off when the turn is complete.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver crashes ahead of you, you should:

options.text: Pull over and yell at them.
Stop safely away from the crash and tell police about the aggressive behavior.
Block the driver in with your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop safely away from the crash and tell police about the aggressive behavior.
questions.explanation: If you see a crash involving an aggressive driver, stop at a safe distance from the scene. Wait for police to arrive and tell them what you saw.

questions.question: If you lose hydraulic brake pressure, you should do all of the following except:
questions.explanation: If your brakes lose pressure, downshift, pump the brakes, and use the parking brake. Look for an escape route like an escape ramp, open field, or side street. Do not accelerate.

questions.question: During the skills test, if you must stop before making a turn, you should:

options.text: Stop after the stop line for a better view.

questions.explanation: Stop smoothly before any stop line or sign. Keep your front wheels pointed straight ahead. Do not let your vehicle roll. Stop where you can see the rear tires of any vehicle in front of you.

questions.question: If your spring brakes are activated, you should never:

options.text: Release air from the air storage tanks.

questions.explanation: Never press the brake pedal when spring brakes are activated. Both springs and air pressure together can damage the brakes.
